Specify a priori expectations for a nomological network

Source: R/nomo_hypotheses.R
nomo_hypotheses.Rd

nomo_hypotheses() converts named theoretical predictions into a machine-readable object that can later be evaluated by nomo_network(). Relations use A -> B for directed structural paths and A <-> B for associations/covariances.

Usage

nomo_hypotheses(...)

Arguments

...

Named nomo_expectations created by positive(), negative(), or negligible(). Names must specify relations using -> or <->.

Value

A nomo_hypotheses object containing a tidy, machine-readable hypothesis table.

Details

The function records theory; it does not inspect data, fit a model, or infer predictions from statistical significance.

Examples

h <- nomo_hypotheses(
  "GSE -> Spirituality" = positive(),
  "GSE -> Religiosity" = negligible(within = c(-.10, .10)),
  "Religiosity <-> Spirituality" = positive(min = .20)
)
h
#> <nomo_hypotheses>
#> 3 theory-specified relation(s)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   id    relation                     prediction region      scale       
#>   <chr> <chr>                        <chr>      <chr>       <chr>       
#> 1 H1    GSE -> Spirituality          positive   (0, +Inf)   standardized
#> 2 H2    GSE -> Religiosity           negligible [-0.1, 0.1] standardized
#> 3 H3    Religiosity <-> Spirituality positive   [0.2, +Inf) standardized
#>   origin  
#>   <chr>   
#> 1 a_priori
#> 2 a_priori
#> 3 a_priori
